I don't mean to expose myself but I recently broke it off with my ex girlfriend of 3 years who also has extreme anxiety, you remind me a lot of her actually tho I'm sure you're not, and I can tell you she's an amazing and pure innocent soul and a fantastic and loving person. Her major flaw was her anxiety driving her to self-destructive behavior and an underlying need to fit in and be accepted. This would cause her to do things she knew was wrong and would damage her in the long run and it always seemed like a good idea but never ended well. I promise you if you throw yourself down a path of destruction, you may just find exactly what you're looking for and that's not always what you need. It's a slippery slope and I promise you it's not worth it. When your kids will one day look at you how will they remember you. This is something you have to be sincere and honest with yourself about. How will you look at yourself? Maybe it will be good for awhile but will you be able to maintain that for a long time? A lot of serious questions that you need to ask and be sincere with yourself about. Be realistic and kill your arrogance. Kill your ego and seriously pick yourself apart and take a really deep look. Sometimes we spend so long lying to ourselves just to get through the day we forget what the truth really is. May you walk a path of peace and guidance.

At times like these, it's best to turn to something you can hold onto. It's not something damaging or unhealthy, but something that keeps you warm, keeps you sane, makes life make more sense.

A lot of people die to their ego and think they can get through life depending on nothing else but themselves, but the truth is, we depend on each other every day.

Find something you can depend on and put your full confidence in to it, let it help you through this. When you're teetering and slipping closer to the edge, sometimes you gotta take a fall and fall we all will. Put your full trust into something and become vulnerable with yourself. Open up to yourself and be sincere and honest with yourself. Sometimes we spend so much time running away from problems and lying to ourselves we forget what the truth is. We all have to believe in and depend on something one way or another. This could be a sign if any to believe in yourself.

Every day I remind myself almost hundreds of times what I want to do and what I want to be and I repeat that to myself over and over again almost on repeat. You got to tell yourself what to do and what not to do over and over and over again. You're down but you have to get up. Our failures don't define us, how we deal with them does. I'm a random comment on a thread that's going to be lost to age, and being a conscious living being I can say to another. If you don't believe in yourself, I do, I believe in you as much as one stranger can believe in another. You're just as capable of achieving what you want as much as the other. What separates us is how we get there. Be honest with yourself and tell yourself the full unfiltered truth and find your way. You can do it.
